title: Rice Wine Explained
description: Rice wine has a long history in East Asia, yet it's often misunderstood and overlooked next to grape wine. Explore its traditions, craftsmanship and modern revival, from how rice is fermented to how to drink it and pair it with food.
topics: Types and styles of rice wine
Hakka culture, food and wine traditions
How to drink and enjoy rice wine

lessons.title: Welcome to Rice Wine Explained
lessons.review:
Rice wine is fermented, not distilled. The big families are Chinese huangjiu (yellow wine, such as Shaoxing), Japanese sake, and Korean makgeolli and cheongju.

Strength usually sits around 6% ABV for makgeolli and around 15–16% for sake.

This course covers rice wine's history, how it is made, its styles, how to drink it, and the Hakka rice wine tradition.

lessons.title: A history of rice wine
lessons.review:
Archaeologists found residue of a fermented drink made with rice, honey and fruit at Jiahu in China dating to around 7000 BCE, among the oldest evidence of alcohol anywhere.

Rice wine became central to ceremony, medicine and cooking across China, then Korea and Japan.

Sake brewing was refined over centuries in Japan's temples and breweries into the precise craft it is today.

questions.explain: Jiahu residue dates to about 7000 BCE.

lessons.title: How rice wine is made
lessons.review:
Rice is polished, washed, soaked and steamed. A mould (koji in Japan, qu in China) turns its starch into sugar.

Yeast ferments that sugar into alcohol at the same time. In sake this is called multiple parallel fermentation.

The mash is pressed, filtered or left cloudy, sometimes pasteurised, and rested before bottling.

lessons.title: Types and styles of rice wine
lessons.review:
Sake grades follow how much the rice is polished: ginjo uses rice polished to 60% or less, daiginjo to 50% or less, and junmai means no added alcohol.

Huangjiu ranges from dry to sweet and is often aged. Makgeolli is milky, lightly sparkling and low in alcohol.

Mijiu is a clear Chinese rice wine, and Hakka families make a sweet glutinous rice wine at home.

lessons.title: How to drink rice wine
lessons.review:
Premium sake is best lightly chilled to show its fragrance; richer styles can be served at room temperature or gently warmed.

Huangjiu is often warmed, sometimes with dried plum or ginger. Makgeolli is shaken gently and served cold.

Rice wine loves food: try it with dumplings, seafood, grilled meats and cheese.

questions.explain: Shake gently to mix the sediment.

lessons.title: Hakka culture: food and wine
lessons.review:
The Hakka people of southern China have a long tradition of brewing sweet glutinous rice wine at home.

It is part of family life and celebrations, and is used generously in cooking, from rice wine chicken to braises.

Hakka rice wine shows how closely food, family and drink are tied together in rice wine culture.
